summary: A Meta AI staffer describes serving-engineering details of a model that quantizes weights to ~4-bit to fit under 20GB alongside its KV cache, perception encoder, and a 'dflash' drafter that proposes token blocks for parallel verification.

mechanisms.reason: Quantizing weights to 4-bit and using a speculative-decoding-style drafter reduces the compute and memory required per token, a stated technique with a concrete figure.
mechanisms.quote: to achieve maximum memory efficiency, we quantize model weights to ~4-bit, getting the language model under 20GB with room for the kv cache, perception encoder, and drafter alongside it

practices.reason: The quantization approach and parallel-verification drafter are concrete techniques an engineering team could reproduce to cut memory footprint and improve throughput.
practices.quote: a dflash drafter proposes blocks of tokens the main model verifies in parallel
